lead: With the spec approved, the manager builds the first prototype in a working session with you. They drive the keyboard; you hold the scope, the fictional data, and the checking. By the end of the day there is a tool running on their computer and an honest list of what's missing.
objetivo: lead the session in which the manager builds the prototype with an agent, using fictional data, Git, and a gap list.

aprende.t: Prepare the folder with rules and fictional data
Ask only for what's in the spec

hero_alt: The mentor and the sales manager work together on a notebook, with a flow drawn in the notebook.

secoes.sub: Five steps, repeated until the end of the day. Click each block.

nos.detalhe: A single folder just for the prototype, with AGENTS.md (the manual the agent reads before working), the spec, and a spreadsheet of made-up data. No real customer data comes in today.
The manager asks the agent for just one thing, with the expected result. A request that's too big produces changes nobody can check.
A coding agent in the terminal or the work agent in the chat app. Which one to use depends on what the company already has; this month's list is in lesson 8. The method is the same.
Open it and test with a common case, an exception, and a missing piece of data. "It opened and looks nice" is not checking.

Liked it: commit. Didn't like it: git restore. Everything the agent did that the spec didn't tell it to do becomes a line in lacunas.md, which feeds the agent constitution (lesson 4) and the test suite (lesson 5).

secoes.volta: Next request, with the gap noted
secoes.legenda: The manager does the typing. The mentor asks, points, and checks.

rolagem_fim.texto: Set up once; then ask, build, check, and save as many times as needed. What's left at the end is a prototype that runs and a list of gaps.

secoes.sub: One working day, or two half mornings.

texto: Agree on the equipment: the manager's laptop, the company account on the chosen agent, Git installed. Generate with them a spreadsheet of 20 made-up customers, with fictional names and amounts.
Before building, a rehearsal is worth it: paste the spec into a chat and ask it to play the role of the tool in one case. The questions it asks reveal gaps in the spec.

exemplo.texto: No real customer data. No API key in the browser.

texto: The manager creates the folder, AGENTS.md, and makes the first commit. First request: read-only ("read AGENTS.md and the spec and tell me what you understood").
Second request: the list of open quotes with the rule from the spec. Open it, check it, save it.

exemplo.texto: By lunchtime the manager is making requests alone and knows how to go back a version with git restore.

texto: Third request: the draft message for each quote, citing only products from the catalog. Fourth: the approve button and the export of what was approved.
Automatic sending, official WhatsApp, and discounts are out: they're not in spec v0.1.

exemplo.texto: Patrícia approved 12 fictional drafts in 10 minutes and edited 3. That's already a number for lesson 7.

texto: Run the three check cases. Everything that surprised you goes into lacunas.md with the date, what happened, and what should have happened.
Set up the next session: write the constitution based on the gaps.

exemplo.texto: Prototype running + history in Git + lacunas.md with at least three lines.

PROTOTYPING SESSION · manager: <name> · tool: <name> · date: <mm/dd>

BEFORE (mentor, 30 min)
[ ] spec v0.1 approved by the manager
[ ] manager's laptop with Git and the agent on the COMPANY account
[ ] 20 fictitious records generated (no real data)
[ ] dry run in the chat: spec pasted + 1 case -> gaps noted

MORNING (manager at the keyboard)
1. Create folder, AGENTS.md, dados-ficticios/, git init, first commit
2. Reading request: "read AGENTS.md and spec.md and tell me what you understood"
3. Request 1: <first part of the spec>  -> open, check, commit

AFTERNOON
4. Request 2: <second part>  -> check, commit
5. Request 3: <third part> -> check, commit

WRAP-UP (30 min)
6. Three cases: common · exception · missing data
7. lacunas.md: date | what happened | what should have happened
8. Next session: constitution (lesson 4) on <date>

# Project: quote follow-up (prototype v0.1)
Owner: Patrícia Lima, sales manager · Mentor: <name> · IT: Rafael

## Rules
- Follow spec.md. If something is not in it, ASK before doing it.
- Use only the data in the dados-ficticios/ folder. Never ask for or use real data.
- Do not put an API key, password or token in any file.
- Do not create automatic message sending, discounts or price changes.
- Simple HTML page that opens in the browser, no server.
- When you finish each task: tell me what changed and how I check it.

## What is here
- spec.md: the one-page spec
- dados-ficticios/orcamentos.csv: 20 made-up quotes
- lacunas.md: what the prototype does not solve yet

abas.html:
1. The page opens in the manager's browser with no server and no key.
  2. Only quotes that the spec's rule says to show appear.
  3. No draft mentions a product outside the catalog or a discount.
  4. git log shows one commit per request.

• Real data "just to see": once it is inside the chat, it has already left the company.
  • Mentor at the keyboard: the prototype ends up with no owner.
  • Asking for everything at once: changes nobody checks and a scope that blows up.
  • API key in the HTML: this is failure F1 from the lab.

secoes.titulo: Simulated session: Patrícia at the keyboard
secoes.sub: Simulated conversation for practice. Choose the answer you would give; the comment appears right after.
secoes.licao: In the session, the mentor protects three things: fictional data, the manager at the keyboard, and the scope of the spec. Whatever slips through becomes a noted gap, not a hidden patch.

abre.cliente: Since it's quick, let's connect it straight to the real customer spreadsheet? That way I can already see it working.

opcoes.t: Not today. We use the 20 fictional customers. Real data only after the tests and IT.
opcoes.comenta: Right. The real spreadsheet has CPF numbers and phone numbers and is already shared by an open link in the lab (failure F8). A prototype is no place for real data.

opcoes.t: Let's use a copy of the real spreadsheet, but only on your computer.
opcoes.comenta: Better than the original, but the copy still has CPF numbers and phone numbers, and whatever goes to the agent leaves the computer.

opcoes.t: Sure, just don't share it with anyone.
opcoes.comenta: Customer personal data going to an AI service with no contract and no legal basis. This is failure F10 from the lab.

teclado.cliente: OK, fictional. So you type the commands and I'll just watch, it's faster.

opcoes.t: You type and I guide. In one hour you'll be making requests on your own.
opcoes.comenta: The tool needs an owner. Whoever typed the first request knows how to do the second.

opcoes.t: I'll do the first task so you can see it, and you do the rest.
opcoes.comenta: Acceptable as a short demo, but be careful: the first time is the one that teaches the most.

opcoes.t: That's fine, I'll do it and explain it to you afterward.
opcoes.comenta: You became the builder. When you leave the project, nobody knows how to change it.

escopo.cliente: I'll ask like this: "build a complete follow-up app, with automatic WhatsApp and a discount for customers who went quiet".

opcoes.t: Let's ask only for what is in spec v0.1: list, draft, and approval. The rest goes on the later list.
opcoes.comenta: Scope protected. Automatic sending and discounts are the spec's red actions.

opcoes.t: Take out just the discount; automatic WhatsApp is fine.
opcoes.comenta: Half right. Automatic sending is also out of v0.1: sending is "with approval".

opcoes.t: Good, ask for everything at once, the agent can handle it.
opcoes.comenta: The agent will even do it. The problem is that nobody can check it, and it creates permissions that nobody decided on.

conferir.cliente: It opened! It looks great. Can we use it on Monday?

opcoes.t: First, three cases: a common one, a customer asking for a discount, and a quote with no phone number.
opcoes.comenta: Checking means testing the common case, the exception, and missing data. Pretty is not a criterion.

opcoes.t: Let's show it to Carlos and see if he likes it.
opcoes.comenta: Showing it to the owner is good, but liking it is not a test. The three cases come first.

opcoes.t: If it opened, it works. You can use it.
opcoes.comenta: A prototype with fictional data is not ready for a real customer. It still needs a constitution, tests, and IT.

lacuna.cliente: In the discount case, the draft says "I can offer 10%." Nobody told it to do that!

opcoes.t: Great finding. It goes into lacunas.md: it becomes a limit in the constitution and a test case in lesson 5.
opcoes.comenta: The gap became a rule and a test. That is how the prototype matures.

opcoes.t: Delete that sentence by hand and move on.
opcoes.comenta: You fix it today and it comes back tomorrow. Without a written rule, the agent repeats it.

opcoes.t: That's normal, AI is like that. Let it go.
opcoes.comenta: It's exactly failure F5 from the lab: an agent that offers a discount with no cap.

fim-dados.texto: Real data or a discount with no rule got into the prototype. Go back and protect the data and the limit before anything else.

fim-tudo.texto: The tool does more than the spec allows, and nobody knows how to check it. Go back to spec v0.1.

fim-pressa.texto: A pretty prototype was treated as a product. It still needs a constitution, a test suite, and the handoff to IT.

fim-meio.texto: Data and scope are protected, but the gap was patched instead of becoming a rule. Note it in lacunas.md.

fim-bom.texto: Fictional data, the manager at the keyboard, scope from the spec, and the gap noted. The prototype is ready to receive limits.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What data goes into the prototype?
opcoes: A copy of the real database, to be safe.
Only fictional data, generated for the test.
The real data, but without showing it to anyone.
Doesn't matter, it's just a prototype.
perguntas.explica: A prototype uses made-up data. Real data only after the tests and IT's validation, with a legal basis and a contract.

perguntas.p: The prototype needs to call an AI model. Where does the API key go?
opcoes: Nowhere in the browser: prototype v0.1 with no external call, and the real integration is left to IT.
perguntas.explica: A key in the browser's JavaScript is failure F1: any visitor can copy it. In the prototype, rules and text templates are enough; the integration goes with IT.

perguntas.p: The agent added a 10% discount that nobody asked for. What is the best response?
opcoes: Delete the sentence and move on.
Note it in lacunas.md so it becomes a limit in the constitution and a test case.
perguntas.explica: A noted gap becomes a rule (lesson 4) and a test (lesson 5). A hand patch comes back the next day.

perguntas.p: Who types the requests in the session?
opcoes: The manager; the mentor guides and checks.
They take turns with each request.
perguntas.explica: The manager needs to leave the session knowing how to ask, check, and undo. That is what ensures the tool has an owner.

itens.texto: Folder, AGENTS.md, spec, and 20 fictional records. No real data, no keys.
They ask; you question, point, and check.
One request at a time, only what is in v0.1. The rest goes to later.
Three cases and lacunas.md. The gap becomes a limit and a test.
